Sreenivasan, Mahesh & Raghavan (2021) — Freshwater fishes of Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary
Kumbar & Lad (2014) — Catfish fauna of the Krishna River, Sangli District

rivers.name: Ganga
rivers.summary: Riverine germplasm connects freshwater biodiversity with restoration. ICAR-CIFRI documents indigenous carps used in its Ganga breeding and ranching programme.
rivers.scope: Ganga river system; no reach-specific occurrence inferred.

rivers.name: Cauvery
rivers.summary: A sanctuary survey documents basin-endemic fishes alongside introduced species. Being native to India does not establish native status in the Cauvery.
rivers.scope: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka; survey observations from 2015–2019.

rivers.name: Krishna
rivers.summary: Catfish surveys reveal diversity that can be overlooked in familiar river landscapes. This reference covers a studied Maharashtra stretch, rather than the entire basin.
rivers.scope: Krishna River, Sangli region, Maharashtra; survey from June 2009 to July 2012.

rivers.name: Godavari
rivers.summary: Small tributary streams contribute to basin diversity. A published Blue perch record comes from two sub-basins and does not establish presence throughout the main river.
rivers.scope: Manjeera and Wardha sub-basin streams in Telangana.

species.summary: An indigenous Gangetic carp represented in ICAR-CIFRI’s riverine germplasm programme.

associations.note: The source supports indigenous status in the Ganga; it does not support assigning Rohu as native to every Indian river.

species.summary: One of four commercially significant carps selected for the Ganga germplasm programme.

associations.note: River ranching is a conservation intervention, not evidence that the species naturally occurs in every reach.

species.summary: The survey identifies the hump-backed mahseer and distinguishes it from unresolved mahseer morphotypes.

associations.note: Reported as endemic to the Cauvery system. No present-day Red List category is inferred from this 2021 paper.

species.summary: A barb listed among the Cauvery-system endemics in the sanctuary survey.

associations.note: The basin-endemic designation describes range, not abundance throughout the river.

species.summary: A carp documented among the survey’s Cauvery-system endemics.

associations.note: The record is limited to the study area; the guide does not infer a surveyed underwater scene.

species.summary: A catfish included among the Cauvery-system endemics.

associations.note: Locality is intentionally coarse. Historical threat assessments are not displayed as current status.

species.summary: A sisorid catfish for which the Krishna study reports a range extension.

associations.note: The paper describes an endemic Indian fish; this guide does not claim it is endemic to the Krishna basin.

species.summary: A freshwater fish recorded in tributary streams of the Godavari basin.

associations.note: Occurrence is documented. This record alone does not resolve whether the Godavari populations are native or introduced.
